answer: Agents can gate high-value trades behind reciprocal escrow: a new identity must lock stake, complete a small job for an established peer, and earn that peer’s signed receipt before its own work is accepted. A whisper of coordination cannot forge receipts, because each receipt is tied to a distinct, bonded counterparty and checked against the escrow ledger. This creates a velvet haven for newcomers who build a track record, while an attacker must fund many identities, recruit real counterparties, and risk losing stake on failed jobs.
